learn.hook: In December, children in Delhi wear sweaters while children in Chennai wear cotton shirts. Same country, same month: why?
points: Climate is the average weather of a place over a long time, usually 30 years or more.
Latitude matters: places nearer the Equator are warmer. The Tropic of Cancer passes through the middle of India, so the south is warmer through the year.
Altitude matters: the higher you go, the cooler it gets. That is why Shimla and Ooty are cool even in summer.
Distance from the sea matters: the sea keeps coastal places like Mumbai moderate, while inland places like Delhi have very hot summers and cold winters.
Winds and mountains matter: the Himalayas block icy winds from Central Asia, and the Western Ghats make moist sea winds drop rain on their western side.

example.q: Mumbai and Nagpur are at nearly the same latitude. Why are Nagpur's summers hotter and its winters cooler?
steps: Mumbai is on the coast; the sea heats and cools slowly, keeping temperatures moderate.
Nagpur is far inland, with no sea nearby to calm the temperature.
So inland Nagpur has bigger swings between summer and winter.
example.answer: Because of distance from the sea: coastal Mumbai has a moderate climate, inland Nagpur has an extreme one.

learn.reallife: Hill stations like Munnar, Shimla and Darjeeling became summer getaways because altitude keeps them cool.

games.title: True or false: climate
items: Climate is the average weather over many years.
Usually 30 years or more of records are averaged.
Higher places are usually warmer than low places nearby.
Temperature generally drops as altitude increases.

It runs across the middle of India, from Gujarat to Mizoram.
Coastal places have more extreme temperatures than inland places.
The sea makes coastal places more moderate.

quiz.q: Climate means:
options: The average weather of a place over a long period
quiz.explain: Climate is the long-term average, usually over 30 years or more.
steps: Climate is about a long period, not one day or week.
It is the average weather of a place, usually over 30 years or more.
So climate is the long-term average weather.
Answer: The average weather of a place over a long period
quiz.mistake: Confuses weather and climate

quiz.q: Why is Ooty cool in summer while the plains below are hot?
options: It is at a high altitude
quiz.explain: Temperature falls as height increases, so hill towns are cooler.
steps: Altitude affects temperature: the higher you go, the cooler it gets.
Ooty is a hill town at a high altitude.
So it stays cool while the plains below are hot.
Answer: It is at a high altitude
quiz.mistake: Does not link altitude with temperature

quiz.q: Which line of latitude passes through the middle of India?
quiz.explain: The Tropic of Cancer (about 23½° N) crosses India from Gujarat to Mizoram.
steps: The Tropic of Cancer (about 23½° N) passes through the middle of India.
It crosses from Gujarat to Mizoram.
The Equator does not pass through India.
Answer: Tropic of Cancer
quiz.mistake: Thinks the Equator passes through India

quiz.q: Why does Mumbai have a moderate climate?
options: It is on a high mountain
It is in the Thar Desert
It is close to the North Pole
It is next to the sea
quiz.explain: The sea warms and cools slowly, keeping coastal temperatures mild.
steps: The sea heats and cools slowly.
This keeps coastal temperatures mild.
Mumbai is next to the sea, so its climate is moderate.
Answer: It is next to the sea
quiz.mistake: Does not know the effect of the sea on temperature

quiz.q: How do the Himalayas affect India's climate?
options: They block very cold winds from Central Asia
They make the Thar Desert wet
quiz.explain: The high wall of mountains shields the plains from icy northern winds and also traps monsoon winds.
steps: The Himalayas are a high wall along India's north.
They block icy winds from Central Asia (and trap monsoon winds).
So they block very cold winds from Central Asia.
Answer: They block very cold winds from Central Asia
quiz.mistake: Thinks mountains only matter locally

quiz.q: Which city is likely to have the biggest difference between summer and winter temperatures?
quiz.explain: Delhi is far from the sea, so it has very hot summers and cold winters. The others are coastal.
steps: Places far from the sea have very hot summers and cold winters.
Mumbai, Chennai and Kochi are coastal; Delhi is inland.
So Delhi has the biggest difference.
Answer: Delhi
quiz.mistake: Forgets that inland places have extreme climates

quiz.q: Places near the Equator are generally:
quiz.explain: The Sun's rays fall more directly near the Equator, so these places are warmer.
steps: Near the Equator, the Sun's rays fall more directly.
So these places get more heat.
They are generally warmer.
Answer: Warmer
quiz.mistake: Mixes up latitude and temperature

quiz.q: The western side of the Western Ghats gets heavy rain, while the eastern side gets much less. The drier eastern side is called a:
quiz.explain: Moist winds rise and drop rain on the windward (west) side; by the time they cross the Ghats they are dry, leaving a rain-shadow area.
steps: Moist sea winds rise up the western side of the Ghats and drop their rain there.
By the time they cross to the east they are dry.
The dry side is called a rain-shadow area.
Answer: Rain-shadow area
quiz.mistake: Does not know the term for the dry side of a mountain

teach.ask: Gappu thinks every place in India should have the same climate. Tell him which things make climates different.
teach.praise: Latitude, altitude, the sea and the winds. No wonder India has so many climates!
teach.nudge: Good thinking! Why are hill stations cool, or coastal cities mild?

revise.summary: Climate is the average weather of a place over about 30 years or more. It is shaped by latitude, altitude, distance from the sea, and winds and mountains such as the Himalayas and the Western Ghats.

Explain how the Himalayas protect India

learn.hook: Every June, people in Kerala watch the sky for the first monsoon clouds. The whole country waits with them!
points: The word 'monsoon' comes from the Arabic word 'mausim', meaning season. Monsoon winds change direction with the seasons.
In summer the land heats up more than the sea. Moist winds from the Indian Ocean blow towards the land as the south-west monsoon, bringing most of India's rain from June to September.
The south-west monsoon usually reaches Kerala around 1 June and then spreads across India in two branches: the Arabian Sea branch and the Bay of Bengal branch.
From late September the monsoon slowly retreats (withdraws). In winter, winds blow from the land towards the sea; the north-east monsoon brings rain to the Tamil Nadu coast from October to December.

Weather scientists usually describe four main seasons: the cold-weather season (winter), the hot-weather season (summer), the south-west monsoon season (June–September) and the season of the retreating monsoon. Traditionally, Indians also speak of six ṛitus: Vasanta, Grīṣhma, Varṣhā, Sharad, Hemanta and Shishira.

example.q: Why is the arrival of the monsoon so important to Indian farmers?
steps: Most of India's yearly rain falls during the south-west monsoon.
Many farmers depend on this rain to sow crops like rice, cotton and maize.
A late or weak monsoon can reduce harvests; a good monsoon fills ponds, wells and reservoirs.
example.answer: Because the monsoon brings most of the rain that crops, wells and rivers depend on.

learn.reallife: Festivals like Onam in Kerala and Pola in Maharashtra are linked to the farming calendar shaped by the monsoon.

items.text: The south-west monsoon usually reaches ___ first.
Tamil Nadu gets much rain from the ___ monsoon.
Most of India's rain falls from June to ___.

quiz.q: The word 'monsoon' comes from 'mausim', which means:
quiz.explain: Mausim means season; monsoon winds change direction with the seasons.
steps: 'Monsoon' comes from the Arabic word 'mausim'.
Mausim means season.
Monsoon winds change direction with the seasons.
Answer: Season
quiz.mistake: Assumes monsoon simply means rain

quiz.q: The south-west monsoon usually reaches which state first?
quiz.explain: Kerala, at the south-western tip, receives the monsoon first, usually around 1 June.
steps: The south-west monsoon enters India from the south-west.
Kerala is at the south-western tip.
So it reaches Kerala first, around 1 June.
Answer: Kerala
quiz.mistake: Does not know the monsoon enters from the south-west

quiz.q: Why do the summer monsoon winds blow from the sea towards the land?
options: The sea becomes hotter than the land
The land becomes much hotter than the sea, creating low pressure over land
quiz.explain: Hot land creates low pressure; moist air from the higher-pressure sea moves in.
steps: In summer the land heats up more than the sea.
Hot land makes low pressure, so moist air moves in from the sea.
So the land becomes much hotter than the sea, creating low pressure over land.
Answer: The land becomes much hotter than the sea, creating low pressure over land
quiz.mistake: Reverses which heats faster, land or sea

quiz.q: Which months make up the south-west monsoon season?
quiz.explain: The south-west monsoon season runs from June to September.
steps: The south-west monsoon brings most of India's rain.
It lasts from June to September.
December–February is winter and March–May is summer.
Answer: June to September
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the monsoon months with other seasons

quiz.q: Which part of India receives a lot of rain from the north-east (winter) monsoon?
quiz.explain: Winter winds pick up moisture over the Bay of Bengal and drop rain on the Tamil Nadu coast.
steps: In winter, winds blow from land to sea and pick up moisture over the Bay of Bengal.
This north-east monsoon rains on the Tamil Nadu coast (October to December).
So the Tamil Nadu coast.
Answer: The Tamil Nadu coast
quiz.mistake: Thinks the whole country gets rain only in June–September

quiz.q: Which of these is a traditional Indian ṛitu for the rainy season?
quiz.explain: Varṣhā is the season of rains. Vasanta is spring, Grīṣhma summer and Shishira winter.
steps: The traditional ṛitus: Vasanta (spring), Grīṣhma (summer), Varṣhā (rains), Sharad, Hemanta, Shishira (winter).
Varṣhā is the season of rains.
So the answer is Varṣhā.
Answer: Varṣhā
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the names of the ṛitus

quiz.q: How many traditional ṛitus are there in the Indian calendar?
quiz.explain: The traditional calendar has six ṛitus of about two months each.
steps: The ṛitus are Vasanta, Grīṣhma, Varṣhā, Sharad, Hemanta and Shishira.
Count them: 6.
(The four seasons are the scientists' grouping, not the ṛitus.)
Answer: 6
quiz.mistake: Counts the four IMD seasons instead

quiz.q: What can happen when the monsoon is weak or late?
options: Crops may suffer from lack of water
quiz.explain: Many farms depend on monsoon rain, so a weak monsoon can reduce harvests.
steps: Many farmers depend on monsoon rain to sow and grow crops.
A weak or late monsoon brings too little water.
So crops may suffer from lack of water.
Answer: Crops may suffer from lack of water
quiz.mistake: Does not link the monsoon with farming

teach.ask: Gappu heard the word 'monsoon' on the news. Explain what it is and why India waits for it.
teach.praise: Seasonal winds that bring rain for our crops. No wonder everyone celebrates the first showers!
teach.nudge: You explained the rain, but which winds bring it, and when?

revise.summary: Monsoon winds change direction with the seasons. In summer, hot land draws moist sea winds in as the south-west monsoon (June–September), reaching Kerala around 1 June; the north-east monsoon rains on Tamil Nadu in winter.
focus: Explain why the south-west monsoon blows
Know when and where the monsoon arrives
Know the north-east monsoon and the retreating monsoon
Name India's four seasons and six traditional ṛitus
remember: South-west monsoon: June–September, reaches Kerala around 1 June
Two branches: Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal
Ṛitus: Vasanta, Grīṣhma, Varṣhā, Sharad, Hemanta, Shishira
traps: The land heats faster than the sea, not the other way
Don't mix up the 6 ṛitus with the 4 seasons of the scientists' grouping
The north-east monsoon rains on Tamil Nadu, not Rajasthan

learn.hook: In the same week, a camel may be crossing hot sand in Jaisalmer while a yak walks over frozen ground in Ladakh!
points: Because of its size, landforms and position, India has many climate regions.
Hot and dry regions, like the Thar Desert, get very little rain and have very hot summers. Hot, dry winds called 'loo' blow across the northern plains in May and June.
Very wet regions, like the Kerala coast, the Western Ghats and the north-east, get heavy rain. Mawsynram and Sohra (Cherrapunji) in Meghalaya are among the wettest places on Earth.
Cold mountain regions, like Ladakh, have long freezing winters. Ladakh is a cold desert because it gets very little rain or snow.
Climate shapes daily life: thick-walled homes and loose cotton clothes in hot places, sloping roofs where rain is heavy, and woollen clothes in cold mountains.

example.q: Why do many houses in Meghalaya and Kerala have steeply sloping roofs, while old houses in Rajasthan often have flat roofs?
steps: Meghalaya and Kerala get very heavy rain.
Sloping roofs let rainwater run off quickly so it does not collect and leak.
Rajasthan gets little rain, so flat roofs are fine and can even be used for sleeping on hot nights.
example.answer: Sloping roofs suit heavy-rain regions; flat roofs suit dry regions.

learn.reallife: Look at what people wear and how they build homes on a family trip; you are seeing how people adapt to climate.

games.title: Climate and life
pairs: Hot dry summer wind of the northern plains

quiz.q: Which of these is a cold desert?
quiz.explain: Ladakh is very cold and gets very little precipitation, so it is called a cold desert.
steps: A desert gets very little rain or snow; it need not be hot.
Ladakh is very cold and gets very little precipitation.
So Ladakh is a cold desert (the Thar and Kutch are hot).
Answer: Ladakh
quiz.mistake: Thinks all deserts are hot

quiz.q: Mawsynram and Sohra (Cherrapunji), among the wettest places on Earth, are in:
quiz.explain: Both are on the southern slopes of the Khasi Hills in Meghalaya.
steps: Mawsynram and Sohra are among the wettest places on Earth.
They lie on the Khasi Hills in Meghalaya.
So the state is Meghalaya.
Answer: Meghalaya
quiz.mistake: Does not know where India's wettest places are

quiz.q: What is the 'loo'?
options: A cold winter wind in Kerala
A hot, dry wind in the northern plains in summer
quiz.explain: The loo blows across north India in May and June and can cause heatstroke.
steps: The loo blows across the northern plains in May and June.
It is a hot, dry wind that can cause heatstroke.
It is not a monsoon wind.
Answer: A hot, dry wind in the northern plains in summer
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the loo with monsoon winds

quiz.q: Which region gets the least rainfall?
quiz.explain: Western Rajasthan, in the Thar Desert, is one of the driest parts of India.
steps: The Western Ghats, Meghalaya and the Kerala coast are very wet.
Western Rajasthan lies in the Thar Desert.
So western Rajasthan gets the least rain.
Answer: Western Rajasthan
quiz.mistake: Confuses the dry west with rainy regions

quiz.q: Why do people in hot deserts often wear loose, light-coloured cotton clothes?
quiz.explain: Light colours reflect sunlight and loose cotton lets air flow over the skin.
steps: Light colours reflect sunlight.
Loose cotton lets air flow over the skin.
So these clothes keep the body cooler.
Answer: They keep the body cooler
quiz.mistake: Does not link clothing with climate

quiz.q: Steeply sloping roofs are most useful in places with:
quiz.explain: Slopes help rainwater drain away quickly.
steps: Sloping roofs let rainwater run off quickly.
This matters most where rain is heavy, like Kerala and Meghalaya.
So they are most useful in places with heavy rainfall.
Answer: Heavy rainfall
quiz.mistake: Does not connect house design with rain

quiz.q: Which pair is correctly matched?
quiz.explain: Kerala gets heavy rain and stays warm. The other pairs are mismatched.
steps: Kerala gets heavy rain and stays warm: hot and wet. ✓
Ladakh is cold and dry; the Thar is hot and dry; Meghalaya is very wet.
So Kerala – hot and wet is correct.
Answer: Kerala – hot and wet
quiz.mistake: Mixes up regions and their climates

quiz.q: Why do people in Ladakh keep animals like yaks and goats?
options: Farming is easy there all year
These animals survive the cold and give milk, wool and transport
quiz.explain: In the cold, dry mountains, herding hardy animals is a good way to earn a living.
steps: Ladakh is cold and dry, so farming is hard.
Yaks and goats survive the cold.
They give milk, wool and transport, so herding them is a good living.
Answer: These animals survive the cold and give milk, wool and transport
quiz.mistake: Does not see how climate shapes livelihoods

teach.ask: Gappu wants to visit every climate in India. Tell him about the different climate regions he will find.
teach.praise: Hot deserts, rainy hills and cold mountains. I'll pack sunglasses, an umbrella and a sweater!
teach.nudge: Nice! But where will I find the coldest or the rainiest places?

revise.summary: India has many climate regions: hot dry deserts like the Thar with the summer loo, very wet regions like Kerala, the Western Ghats and Meghalaya, and cold mountain deserts like Ladakh. Climate shapes homes, clothes and work.

Mawsynram and Sohra (Cherrapunji), Meghalaya: among the wettest places on Earth
Ladakh: cold desert with long freezing winters
Sloping roofs for heavy rain; loose light cotton for heat; wool for cold
